questions.stem: A translator's note: f(x)=x^{2/3}; how many critical points on R?
questions.explanation: f'= (2/3)x^{-1/3}, undefined at 0, zero nowhere, so x=0 is the only critical point (cusp minimum). The tempting 0 count misses the cusp.

questions.subject: ALGEBRA_II
questions.stem: A translator's note: f(x)=x^3; inflection point?
questions.explanation: f''=6x, sign changes at 0, so (0,0) is an inflection point. It is not a min/max. The tempting none or minimum are wrong.

questions.subject: ALGEBRA_II
questions.learningObjective: Classify point where f'=0 and f''>0
questions.stem: A translator's note: at x=a, f'(a)=0 and f''(a)>0; explain the conclusion.

answer.exemplar: The point is a local minimum: stationary with positive second derivative means concave up, so the curve bottoms out at (a,f(a)).

questions.explanation: f'=0 gives stationary; f''>0 gives concave up; together a local minimum. The tempting maximum reverses the sign.

questions.subject: ALGEBRA_II
questions.learningObjective: Find local min value of quartic
questions.stem: A translator's note: f(x)=x^4-4x^2; first find critical points, then local min value.
questions.explanation: f'=4x^3-8x=4x(x^2-2); critical 0,±√2. f(±√2)=4-8=-4 (min), f(0)=0 (max). Local min value -4. The tempting values use wrong critical points.
